questions.q: Given below is a map of some countries which were parts of the erstwhile Soviet Union, with water bodies shown by shaded areas: [1995] 1️⃣ The countries marked 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are respectively:
questions.e: According to the map of the former Soviet Union republics in Central Asia, the correct identification for the numbers is: 1-Kazakhstan, 2-Turkmenia, 3-Uzbekistan, 4-Kirgizia, and 5-Tajikistan.

questions.q: The standard time of the following countries is ahead of or behind Greenwich Mean Time depending on whether they are East or West of the longitude passing through Greenwich. [1995] 1️⃣ Cuba 2️⃣ Greece 3️⃣ Ira️⃣ Costa Rica 5️⃣ Japan. Which one of the following sequential orders gives the correct arrangement of the countries according to their standard time from ahead to behind GMT?
questions.e: Time is ahead of GMT for countries to the East and behind for those to the West. Japan is furthest East, followed by Iraq and Greece. Cuba and Costa Rica are to the West, with Costa Rica being further West than Cuba.

questions.q: The original home of the gypsies was: [1995]
questions.e: While Gypsies (Roma) are found across Central Asia and Europe, their original ancestral home is tracked back to India, specifically the Western Rajasthan and Punjab regions. They began their wandering lifestyle during the late middle ages.

questions.q: Consider the map given below indicating four places frequently figuring in the news: [1995] 1️⃣ Which one of them is Chechenya?
questions.e: Chechnya is situated in the Asian continent as a federal subject of Russia. It was frequently in the news during the mid-1990s due to separatist movements and conflict.

questions.q: Arakan Yoma is the extension of the Himalayas located in: [1995]
questions.e: Arakan Yoma is a mountain range in western Myanmar. It serves as an eastern extension of the Himalayan system and includes the Naga hills, Chin hills, and Patkai range.

questions.q: Consider the map given below: [1996] 1️⃣ The dotted (broken) line in the map is the:
o: Line of demarcation between India and Pakistan suggested by the Boundary Commission (1947)
Route followed by young husband's expedition
questions.e: The dotted line represents the Durand Line, which serves as the boundary between India (now Pakistan region) and Afghanistan. It was demarcated by a commission led by Mortimer Durand in 1896.

questions.q: Which one of the following regions of India is now regarded as an 'ecological hot spot'? [1996]
questions.e: The Western Ghats is recognized as a major ecological hot spot in India. It was notified for its high level of biodiversity and endemism under the Wild Life Act.

questions.q: The rough outline map shows a portion of the Middle East. 1️⃣ The countries labelled A, B, C and D are respectively: [1996]
o: Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia and Jordan
Iraq, Syria, Saudi Arabia and Jordan
Iraq, Syria, Jordan and Saudi Arabia
Syria, Iraq, Jordan and Saudi Arabia
questions.e: Based on the geographical layout of the Middle East map provided, label 'A' represents Iraq, 'B' is Syria, 'C' is Saudi Arabia, and 'D' is Jordan.

questions.q: The Palk Bay lies between: [1996]
o: Gulf of Kutch and Gulf of Khambhat
Gulf of Mannar and Bay of Bengal
questions.e: The Palk Bay (or Palk Strait) is the body of water that separates India and Sri Lanka. Geographically, it is positioned between the Gulf of Mannar to the southwest and the Bay of Bengal to the northeast.

questions.q: A rough outline map of northern Sri Lanka is shown below. 1️⃣ Jaffna is located at the point marked: [1996]
questions.e: Point 'D' on the northern tip of the Sri Lankan map indicates the location of Jaffna. This area was historically significant as a stronghold for the LTTE group.

questions.q: About 50% of the world population is concentrated between the latitudes of: [1997]
questions.e: Half of the global population resides between 20°N and 40°N latitude. This is because major population centers in Asia (including India and China), Europe, and the USA fall within this belt.

questions.q: ".....They are people of yellow complexion, oblique eyes, high check bones, sparse hair and medium height." 1️⃣ The reference here is to: [1997]
questions.e: These physical characteristics—yellowish skin, epicanthic folds (oblique eyes), high cheekbones, and medium stature—are defining traits of the Mongoloid race, which includes populations in China, Japan, Myanmar, and Vietnam.

questions.q: Consider the map given below: [1997] 1️⃣ The river shown on the map is:
questions.e: The river depicted in the eastern part of Myanmar is the Salween. It originates in the Shan Plateau and forms part of the border between Myanmar (Burma) and Thailand.

questions.q: "From Aceh in the far north west to Torres Strait in the east is 5000 miles, almost as far as from London to Baghdad. 1️⃣ The archipelago has 14,000 islands, some mere equatorial rocks, others some of the largest in the world." This description best fits: [1997]
questions.e: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago, consisting of approximately 13,677 to 14,000 islands. Its vast extent from Aceh to the Torres Strait covers a distance comparable to that between London and Baghdad.

questions.q: Consider the geographical details given in the following figure: [1997] 1️⃣ The point marked by A in the above figure indicates the countries in:
questions.e: The coordinates (around 51°N) and the air route details provided in the figure correspond to the location of England, which is situated in the continent of Europe.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is the largest producer of fuel wood in the world? [1997]
questions.e: Based on FAO data cited in the text, India is the leading producer of fuel wood, with a production of approximately 305 million cubic metres, followed by China and Indonesia.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries has replaced Italy as the major importer of bauxite from India? [1998]
questions.e: Historical trade data from the late 1990s indicates that Canada became the primary destination for Indian bauxite exports, taking over the position previously held by Italy.

questions.q: Indonesian forest fire in 1997 was caused by: [1998]
questions.e: The severe 1997 Indonesian forest fires were primarily driven by the El Niño effect, which caused extreme drought conditions, though human negligence in land clearing for plantations (pulpwood and palm oil) also played a major role.

questions.q: When there is noon at I.S.T. meridian people at another place of the earth are taking their 6 O' clock morning tea. 1️⃣ The longitude of the place is: [1998]
questions.e: The difference between 12:00 PM (IST) and 6:00 AM is 6 hours. Since 15° longitude equals 1 hour, 6 hours equals 90°. IST is at 82°30' E. Subtracting 90° from 82°30' E puts the location at 7°30' W.

questions.q: Which one of the following port cities in Venezuela has been developed as an oil port? [1999]
questions.e: Puerto Miranda, located on the eastern side of Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela, serves as a major oil port and is the largest crude oil export facility in South America.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Chile continues to be an important producer of copper in the world. 1️⃣ Reason (R): Chile is endowed with the world's largest deposit of porphyry copper. [1999]
o: Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.e: Chile is the world's leading copper producer, accounting for about 35% of global output. This dominance is directly attributed to its massive deposits of porphyry copper.

questions.q: Match the cities labelled as A, B, C and D in the given map with the names of cities: 1️⃣ A-Darwin 2️⃣ B-Kualalumpur 3️⃣ C-Lagos 4️⃣ D-Nairobi [1999]
questions.e: On the map of the world/Indian Ocean region: 'A' is Darwin (Australia), 'B' is Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), 'C' is Nairobi (Kenya), and 'D' is Lagos (Nigeria).

questions.q: A person of mixed European and Indian blood in Latin America is called a: [1999]
questions.e: The term 'Mestizo' historically refers to individuals of combined European (Spanish/Portuguese) and Indigenous American Indian descent in Latin American societies.

questions.q: Match List-I (Volcanic Mountain) with List-II (Country): 1️⃣ Mt. Rainier-USA 2️⃣ Etna-Italy 3️⃣ Paricutin-Mexico 4️⃣ Taal-Philippines [1999]
questions.e: The correct pairings are: Mt. Rainier is located in the USA; Mt. Etna is a famous volcano in Italy (Europe); Paricutin is in Mexico; and Taal is in the Philippines.

questions.q: Consider the following provinces of former Yugoslavia: 1️⃣ Bosnia 2️⃣ Croatia 3️⃣ Slovenia 4️⃣ Yugoslavia. 1️⃣ The correct sequence of these provinces from the east to west is: [2000]
questions.e: Geographically, moving from East to West across the former Yugoslavia, the order is Yugoslavia (Serbia/Montenegro), followed by Bosnia, then Croatia, and finally Slovenia in the far West.

questions.q: Which one of the following lakes forms an international boundary between Tanzania and Uganda? [2000]
questions.e: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa and acts as a natural international boundary between Tanzania and Uganda (and Kenya). It is the second-widest freshwater body globally.

questions.q: A class of animals known as Marsupials is a characteristic feature of: [2001]
questions.e: Marsupials are mammals characterized by a pouch where they nurse their young. Australia is the primary home for these animals, with famous examples being the Kangaroo and Koala.

questions.q: The map provided shows the Union Territory of: [2001]
questions.e: The specific map outline represents Dadra and Nagar Haveli in Western India. Its capital is Silvassa, and the major language spoken in the territory is Gujarati.

questions.q: Match List-I (Local Wind) with List-II (Region): 1️⃣ Fohn-Alps 2️⃣ Sarmun-Kurdistan 3️⃣ Santa Ana-California 4️⃣ Zonda-Argentina [2001]
questions.e: Fohn is a warm dry wind in the Alps. Sarmun is local to Kurdistan. Santa Ana is a famous dry wind in California, and Zonda occurs in Argentina.

questions.q: The given map shows four towns of Central Asian region marked as 1, 2, 3 and 4. Identify these towns: [2001]
questions.e: On the map of Central Asian towns: 1 is Ashkhabad (Turkmenistan), 2 is Tashkent (Uzbekistan), 3 is Bishkek (Kyrgyzstan), and 4 is Dushanbe (Tajikistan).

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding environment issues in India: 1️⃣ Gulf of Mannar is one of the biosphere reserves. 2️⃣ The Ganga Action Plan, phase II has been merged with the National River Conservation Plan. 3️⃣ The National Museum of Natural History at New Delhi imparts non-formal education in environment and conservation. 4️⃣ Environmental Information System (ENVIS) acts as a decentralized information network. [2001]
questions.e: All statements are correct. The Gulf of Mannar is a significant biosphere reserve. The Ganga Action Plan II was integrated into the NRCP. The New Delhi Museum focuses on non-formal education, and ENVIS serves as a decentralized network for environmental data.

questions.q: Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Brazil 2️⃣ Indonesia 3️⃣ Japan 4️⃣ Russia. 1️⃣ What is the descending order of the size of the following countries population-wise? [2002]
questions.e: Based on 2000 population data: Indonesia (213 million) > Brazil (176 million) > Russia (146 million) > Japan (126 million).

questions.q: Consider the following countries of South Asia: 1️⃣ Bangladesh 2️⃣ India 3️⃣ Pakistan 4️⃣ Sri Lanka. 1️⃣ The descending order of literacy status of these countries is: [2002]
questions.e: Literacy rates (UNESCO 2015) show Sri Lanka at the top (92.6%), followed by India (72.1%), then Bangladesh (72.8% - though figures vary, Sri Lanka is consistently highest), and Pakistan (56.4%). Note: Some records place Bangladesh slightly above/below India, but 4 is always first and 3 is last.

questions.q: Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Albania 2️⃣ Bosnia Herzegovina 3️⃣ Croatia 4️⃣ Macedonia. 1️⃣ Which of these countries has/have Adriatic Sea as a boundary? [2002]
questions.e: Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, and Croatia all have coastlines on the Adriatic Sea. Macedonia is landlocked and does not share a boundary with the Adriatic.

questions.q: In the map given below, four islands of Indian Ocean region: 1️⃣ Seychelles 2️⃣ Chagos 3️⃣ Mauritius 4️⃣ Socotra are marked as 1, 2, 3 and 4. Match them: [2002]
questions.e: In the Indian Ocean map: 1 is Chagos, 2 is Socotra, 3 is Seychelles, and 4 is Mauritius.

questions.q: The waterfall 'Victoria' is associated with the river: [2003]
questions.e: Victoria Falls, one of the world's largest waterfalls, is located on the Zambezi River in Africa, on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.

questions.q: Life expectancy is the highest in the world in: [2003]
questions.e: Japan consistently records the highest life expectancy globally (over 80 years), surpassing other developed nations like Canada, Norway, and Germany.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In Macedonia, ethnic Albanians are in a minority. 2️⃣ In Kosovo, Serbians are in a majority. 1️⃣ Which of these statements is/are correct? [2003]
questions.e: In Macedonia, ethnic Albanians comprise a significant minority (approx 23%). In Kosovo, the situation is reversed: ethnic Albanians are the vast majority (92%), while Serbians are the minority.

questions.q: Israel has common borders with: [2003]
questions.e: Israel shares land borders with four countries: Lebanon to the north, Syria to the northeast, Jordan to the east, and Egypt to the southwest.

questions.q: Which among the following countries has the largest population? [2003]
questions.e: Among the options provided, Indonesia has the largest population, being the fourth most populous country in the world.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is land locked? [2003]
questions.e: Bolivia is a landlocked country in South America, surrounded by Peru, Chile, Argentina, Brazil, and Paraguay.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does not border the Caspian Sea? [2003]
questions.e: The Caspian Sea is bordered by Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Russia, and Iran. Armenia is a landlocked country in the Caucasus and does not touch the Caspian Sea.

questions.q: The great Asian river Mekong does not run through: [2004]
questions.e: The Mekong flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam. It does not flow through Malaysia.

questions.q: Latvia does not share its borders with which one of the following countries? [2004]
questions.e: Latvia is bordered by Estonia to the north, Lithuania to the south, Russia to the east, and Belarus to the southeast. It does not share a border with Poland.

questions.q: Match List-I (Sea) with List-II (Country): 1️⃣ Black Sea-Bulgaria 2️⃣ Red Sea-Eritrea 3️⃣ Yellow Sea-China 4️⃣ Caspian Sea-Kazakhstan [2004]
questions.e: Bulgaria borders the Black Sea. Eritrea has a coastline on the Red Sea. The Yellow Sea borders China. Kazakhstan is one of the countries bordering the Caspian Sea.

questions.q: Which one of the following does not border Panama? [2004]
questions.e: Panama is an isthmus bordering Costa Rica to the west and Colombia to the east. It is situated between the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. Venezuela does not border it.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries does not border Lithuania? [2005]
questions.e: Lithuania is bordered by Latvia, Belarus, Poland, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. Ukraine is separated from Lithuania by Belarus and Poland.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the given towns of Pakistan while moving from the north towards the south? [2005]
questions.e: Moving from north to south in Pakistan, the sequence of major towns is Peshawar, followed by the capital Islamabad, then Gujranwala, and finally Multan in the south.

questions.q: Match List-I (City) with List-II (River): 1️⃣ Washington, D.C.-Potomac 2️⃣ Berlin-Spree 3️⃣ Paris-Seine 4️⃣ Madrid-Manzanares [2005]
questions.e: Washington, D.C. is on the Potomac. Berlin is located on the Spree. Paris is famous for the Seine, and Madrid is situated on the Manzanares.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Great Britain comprises England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland. 2️⃣ England covers less than 60% of the total area of the United Kingdom. 1️⃣ Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2005]
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect because Great Britain includes only England, Wales, and Scotland; the United Kingdom includes Northern Ireland. Statement 2 is correct; England covers about 53% of the UK's total land area.

questions.q: Itaipu Dam built on the river Parana is one of the largest dams in the world. 1️⃣ Which of the following two countries have this as a joint project? [2005]
questions.e: The Itaipu Dam, located on the Paraná River at the border between Brazil and Paraguay, is a massive hydroelectric project operated jointly by both nations.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the given continents in the decreasing order of their percentage of Earth's land? [2005]
questions.e: The correct order by land area is Africa (29.8m sq km), followed by North America (21.5m sq km), South America (17.5m sq km), and Europe (9.6m sq km).

questions.q: Bermuda Triangle extends up to which of the following places? 1️⃣ Southern Florida 2️⃣ Puerto Rico 3️⃣ Hawaiian Islands [2006]
questions.e: The Bermuda Triangle is a region in the North Atlantic Ocean defined by points in Bermuda, Puerto Rico, and Fort Lauderdale (Southern Florida). It does not include the Hawaiian Islands.

questions.q: Claims to the historical Macedonian territory have been a bone of contention between which of the following countries? [2006]
questions.e: Bulgaria and Greece have historically disputed the territory of Macedonia, a conflict stemming from competing nationalist claims in the Balkan region.

questions.q: Huangpu River flows through which one of the following cities? [2006]
questions.e: The Huangpu River is the most important waterway in Shanghai, China, serving as the city's main source of drinking water and a major shipping lane.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries is the leading producer of uranium? [2006]
questions.e: While Kazakhstan is currently the world's top producer, among the options provided (and based on data at the time of the question), Canada was the leading producer.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Length of a terrestrial mile is lesser than that of a nautical mile. 2️⃣ Harmattan is a dusty land-wind of the East African Coast. 3️⃣ Greece and Albania form a part of the Iberian Peninsula. 1️⃣ Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct? [2006]
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct (1 terrestrial mile = 1609m, 1 nautical mile = 1852m). Statement 2 is incorrect; Harmattan blows on the West African coast. Statement 3 is incorrect; Greece and Albania are in the Balkan Peninsula, while the Iberian Peninsula consists of Spain and Portugal.

questions.q: Through which one of the following groups of countries does the Equator pass? [2006]
questions.e: The Equator passes through 13 countries including Colombia, Kenya, and Indonesia. It does not pass through Zambia, Sudan, or Malaysia.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [2006]
questions.e: Baikonur is the world's largest space launch facility, but it is located in Kazakhstan, not Russia (though leased by Russia). The other pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q: Other than India and China, which one of the following groups of countries border Myanmar? [2006]
questions.e: Myanmar (Burma) shares borders with five countries: India, China, Thailand, Laos, and Bangladesh.

questions.q: Where is Copacabana Beach located? [2007]
questions.e: Copacabana is a world-famous beach located in the city of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

questions.q: Which one of the following cities does not have the same clock time as that of the other three cities at any given instant? [2007]
questions.e: London, Lisbon, and Accra are all located near the Prime Meridian (GMT). Addis Ababa is far to the east (38.74°E) and thus has a significantly different clock time.

questions.q: Match List I (City) with List II (River): 1️⃣ Bangkok-Chao Phraya 2️⃣ Phnom-Penh-Mekong 3️⃣ Hanoi-Red River 4️⃣ Yangon-Irrawaddy [2007]
questions.e: Bangkok is on the Chao Phraya (Menam). Phnom Penh is on the Mekong. Hanoi is on the Red River, and Yangon (Rangoon) is on the Irrawaddy.

questions.q: Which one among the following rivers is the longest? [2007]
questions.e: The Amazon River is the longest (or second longest depending on measurement) and largest by water volume in the world, originating in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.q: Through which one of the following Straits, does a tunnel connect the United Kingdom and France? [2007]
questions.e: The Channel Tunnel, which connects the UK and France, passes under the Strait of Dover, the narrowest part of the English Channel.

questions.q: The largest coral reef in the world is found near the coast of: [2007]
questions.e: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, is located off the northeastern coast of Australia.

questions.q: In which one of the following is Malta located? [2008]
questions.e: Malta is an island nation located in the center of the Mediterranean Sea, south of Italy and north of Libya.

questions.q: Which of the following cities is nearest to the equator? [2008]
questions.e: Singapore is located only about 137 km (roughly 1.3°N) north of the Equator, making it the closest city among the options.

questions.q: Which one of the following straits is nearest to the International Date Line? [2008]
questions.e: The Bering Strait, separating Russia and Alaska, is located very close (approx 1.5 km) to the International Date Line.

questions.q: Which of the following countries share borders with Moldova? 1️⃣ Ukraine 2️⃣ Romania 3️⃣ Belarus [2008]
questions.e: Moldova is a landlocked Eastern European country bordered by Romania to the west and Ukraine to the north, east, and south. It does not border Belarus.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ajman is one of the seven emirates of the UAE. 2️⃣ Ras al-Khaimah was the last Sheikhdom to join the UAE. 1️⃣ Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2008]
questions.e: Both are correct. Ajman is indeed one of the 7 emirates. Ras al-Khaimah joined the federation in 1972, making it the final Sheikhdom to join.

questions.q: Which two countries follow China and India in the decreasing order of their population? [2008]
questions.e: In the global population ranking, China is 1st and India is 2nd. They are followed by the United States (3rd) and Indonesia (4th).

questions.q: Through which of the following countries does the Tropic of Capricorn pass? 1️⃣ Australia 2️⃣ Namibia 3️⃣ Brazil 4️⃣ Chile [2009]
questions.e: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through 10 countries: Chile, Argentina, Paraguay, Brazil, Namibia, Botswana, South Africa, Mozambique, Madagascar, and Australia.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched? [2009]
questions.e: Berlin is located on the rivers Spree and Havel, not the Rhine. The other cities are correctly matched with their respective rivers.

questions.q: Which one among the following South Asian countries has the highest population density? [2009]
questions.e: Among these South Asian nations, India has the highest population density (approx 324 persons/sq km), followed by Sri Lanka (280), Pakistan (146), and Nepal (102).

questions.q: Match List I (Geographic feature) with List II (Country): 1️⃣ Great Victoria Desert-Australia 2️⃣ Grand Canyon-USA 3️⃣ Lake Winnipeg-Canada 4️⃣ Southern Alps-New Zealand [2009]
questions.e: Great Victoria Desert is in Australia. Grand Canyon is a famous gorge in the USA. Lake Winnipeg is in Canada, and the Southern Alps mountain range is in New Zealand.

questions.q: Cape Canaveral, the site from which space shuttles are launched is located on the coast of: [2009]
questions.e: Cape Canaveral is a prominent cape on the Atlantic coast of Florida and is home to the Kennedy Space Center.

questions.q: Which among the following has the world's largest reserves of Uranium? [2009]
questions.e: Australia possesses roughly 24% of the world's known uranium reserves, the largest share of any single country.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the country's administrative capital new federal administrative centre of Malaysia? [2009]
questions.e: Putrajaya was established in the late 1990s as the new federal administrative center of Malaysia to ease congestion in Kuala Lumpur.

questions.q: Which one of the following can come across if one travels through the Strait of Malacca? [2010]
questions.e: The Strait of Malacca is a narrow waterway between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra. Singapore is situated at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula along this route.

questions.q: Turkey is located between: [2014-I]
o: Gulf of Suez and Mediterranean Sea
Gulf of Aqaba and Dead Sea
questions.e: Turkey is positioned at the crossroads of Europe and Asia, bordered by the Black Sea to the north and the Mediterranean Sea to the south.

questions.q: Region often in news: 1️⃣ Chechnya-Russian Federation 2️⃣ Darfur-Mali 3️⃣ Swat Valley-Ira️⃣ Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched? [2014-I]
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Chechnya is in Russia. Darfur is actually a region in western Sudan, not Mali. Swat Valley is located in Pakistan, not Iraq.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of occurrence of the following cities in South-East Asia as one proceeds from south to north? 1️⃣ Bangkok 2️⃣ Hanoi 3️⃣ Jakarta 4️⃣ Singapore [2014-I]
questions.e: Moving from south to north: Jakarta (Indonesia) is southernmost, followed by Singapore, then Bangkok (Thailand), and finally Hanoi (Vietnam) in the north.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries of South-West Asia does not open out to the Mediterranean Sea? [2015-I]
questions.e: While Syria, Lebanon, and Israel have coastlines on the Mediterranean, Jordan is nearly landlocked, having only a small outlet to the Red Sea via the Gulf of Aqaba.

questions.q: With reference to the 'Trans-Pacific Partnership', consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an agreement among all the Pacific Rim countries except China and Russia. 2️⃣ It is a strategic alliance for the purpose of maritime security only. 1️⃣ Which of the statements given above is/are correct? [2016-I]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because not *all* Pacific Rim countries are members (only 12 specific nations signed it). Statement 2 is false as TPP is primarily a trade and economic agreement, not just for maritime security.

questions.q: Which of the following is geographically closest to Great Nicobar? [2017-I]
questions.e: Sumatra (Indonesia) is the closest landmass to the Great Nicobar island, situated much nearer than Sri Lanka or other Indonesian islands like Java and Borneo.

questions.q: Mediterranean Sea is a border of which of the following countries? 1️⃣ Jordan 2️⃣ Ira️⃣ Lebanon 4️⃣ Syria. 1️⃣ Select the correct answer using the code given below: [2017-I]
questions.e: Lebanon and Syria border the Mediterranean Sea. Jordan and Iraq are inland relative to the Mediterranean and do not have coastlines on it.

questions.q: Which of the following has/have shrunk immensely/dried up in the recent past due to human activities? 1️⃣ Aral Sea 2️⃣ Black Sea 3️⃣ Lake Baikal [2018-I]
questions.e: The Aral Sea has shrunk to about 10% of its original size due to water diversion for irrigation. While Lake Baikal faces ecological threats, it has not "shrunk immensely" or dried up. The Black Sea remains stable in size.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs (Sea: Bordering country): 1️⃣ Adriatic Sea: Albania 2️⃣ Black Sea: Croatia 3️⃣ Caspian Sea: Kazakhstan 4️⃣ Mediterranean Sea: Morocco 5️⃣ Red Sea: Syria. 1️⃣ Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched? [2019-I]
questions.e: Pairs 1, 3, and 4 are correct. Croatia borders the Adriatic Sea, not the Black Sea. Syria borders the Mediterranean Sea, not the Red Sea.
